title: Serving Runtime: Architecture, Scheduling, Profiling & Ops Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document consolidates the serving runtime reference material: architecture overview, kernel scheduling policy, profiling playbooks, benchmarking suite, release notes, known issues, and operational runbooks. It is intended for engineers who operate or extend the Redwood serving runtime and for SREs executing incident procedures.

Scope and audience
- Audience: runtime engineers, infra/SRE, applied ML teams onboarding models.
- Scope: production serving runtime (hosted/dedicated/private), GPU scheduling, profiling, performance verification, and incident response.

1) Runtime architecture (high-level)

Summary
- The runtime is a modular inference engine composed of: front-end request router, model worker pools (per model-version-quantization), persistent KV-cache service, batching coordinator, and telemetry/observability exporters.
- Design goals: predictable latency (p50/p95 targets), cost-efficient throughput, graceful degradation (fallbacks to cheaper model variants), and deterministic performance across deployment modes.

Components and responsibilities
- API router: handles authentication, routing policy (latency/cost/region tiers), and pre-processing (tokenization, validation). Owned by: eng-platform.
- Batching coordinator: maintains per-worker shaping windows, continuous batching for low-latency workloads, and backpressure when queues exceed thresholds. Owned by: serving-runtime.
- Model workers: GPU processes responsible for kernel selection, execution, KV cache handling, and quantized kernels. Each worker exposes a health port and metrics. Owned by: serving-runtime.
- KV cache service: optional, shared prefix-cache to avoid re-computation of prefix attention states for repeated prompts. Configurable TTL and memory limits per customer. Owned by: eng-platform.
- Telemetry exporters: traces (OpenTelemetry), metrics (Prometheus), logs (structured JSON to ELK), and perf profiles (periodic pprof/Trace).

SLOs and targets (global defaults)
- p50 latency (token): <= 10ms
- p95 latency (token): <= 40ms
- tail latency (99.9th): <= 250ms (target for small tokens)
- throughput per GPU (NVIDIA A100 80GB baseline): 30-50 tokens/sec for gpt-medium style models (depends on sequence length and quantization)
- error budget and alerting: pages for >= 5% 5m error rate or > 15% sustained capacity saturation for 10m.

2) Kernel selection & scheduling policies

Kernel selection rules (worker-local)
- The kernel selector chooses implementation based on: model architecture tag, sequence length distribution, batch size, and quantization profile.
- Preferred kernel ordering: cuda-fused-attn -> cuBLAS-optimized matmul -> fallback reference kernels.
- Quantized paths: INT8/FP16/FP32 kernels are selected at load time; warm start tests validate numerical stability for sample prompts.

GPU scheduling and worker sizing
- Worker per-GPU concurrency defaults: 1 worker per model-family per GPU for large models (>= 70B equiv), 2-4 for medium (7B-20B) using multi-model packing.
- Preemption policy: low-priority (background) workloads may be preempted when sustained latency breach is detected on a GPU for high-priority customers.
- Affinity rules: prefer colocating complementary models (small + large) only if memory headroom > 15% to avoid OOM during long sequences.

Scheduling knobs and tunables (example config table)
| config_key | description | recommended default | notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| scheduling.policy | global scheduling policy (latency|cost|balanced) | balanced | affects routing and preemption behavior |
| worker.max_batch_tokens | max tokens to batch per window | 1024 | tuned per model family |
| worker.shaping_window_ms | continuous batching window | 8 | lower for lower latency workloads |
| kernel.fallback_threshold | measured p99 latency to trigger fallback kernels | 200ms | unit: ms |
| affinity.memory_headroom_pct | required free GPU memory to colocate | 15 | percent |

3) Profiling playbook (how to profile performance regressions)

When to profile
- New model onboarding (first 24h of traffic).
- After any kernel change, third-party lib upgrade (e.g., cuBLAS/cuDNN), or CUDA driver update.
- If p95/p99 latency increases by >10% over baseline for 24h.

Step-by-step profiling procedure
1. Reproduce workload: capture representative request traces (token distribution, prompt lengths, function-calling frequency).
2. Isolate model worker: direct a test shard of traffic to a single worker process or dedicated test GPU.
3. Capture metrics: enable per-request tracing, GPU utilization (nvidia-smi + DCGM), and pprof CPU profiles for 60-120s under steady-state QPS.
4. Collect kernel timelines: use Nsight Systems or CUPTI to get kernel launch times and overlaps.
5. Analyze hot spots: look for long kernels (>5ms), serialization points, blocking synchronizations, or frequent small kernel launches.
6. Tune batch window and kernel selection: incrementally adjust worker.shaping_window_ms and worker.max_batch_tokens and re-run.
7. Validate: run the benchmarking suite (see next section) and compare against baseline.

Helpful commands (examples)
- Capture GPU and DCGM metrics: sudo dcgmi dmon --viewer -o sample.csv -c 60
- Run pprof on a worker PID: go tool pprof -http=:8080 /tmp/pprof_cpu.pb
- Nsight snapshot: nsys profile --stats=true -o /tmp/trace.nsys --pid <worker-pid>

Data to attach to issue
- representative trace (json), pprof CPU profile, Nsight/CUPTI timeline, Prometheus range query for key metrics, model binary hash, worker config, and diff of recent kernel/driver versions.

4) Benchmarking suite (continuous and ad-hoc)

Goals
- Provide reproducible performance baselines for each model variant, quantization profile, and hardware SKU.
- Verify end-to-end latency and throughput under realistic workload shapes (prompt length, streaming enabled/disabled).

Test types
- Microbenchmarks: token-level latency for single-request steady state; measures kernel performance in isolation.
- Macrobenchmarks: realistic QPS with mixed prompt-length distributions, streaming enabled, function-calling scenarios.
- Stress tests: long-tail prompts, burst traffic patterns, and sustained high QPS to validate autoscaling and fallback policies.

Benchmarking workflow
1. Define scenario YAML: includes model-version, quantization profile, hardware SKU, sequence length distribution, and latency/throughput targets. (Example YAML in Appendix).
2. Run tests on canary pool with the same routing rules as production.
3. Record: prometheus metrics, end-to-end traces, and raw per-request latencies.
4. Compare against baseline using stored golden traces and generate regression report.
5. Gate release if any critical regressions (p95 regression > 15% or p99 regression > 10%).

Artifacts and storage
- All benchmark results are stored in the performance-results bucket: s3://redwood-performance/benchmarks/YYYY-MM-DD/<scenario>.json
- Regression dashboards are auto-generated and linked to PRs.

5) Release notes (recent notable changes)

2026-03-12 (v2026.03.12) - serving-runtime
- Fixed: kernel selection bug where short-sequence workloads incorrectly selected fused-attn, causing 2x latency in edge cases.
- Improved: batching coordinator algorithm (shaping window adaptation) reduced p95 by ~12% on med-size models.
- Added: new INT8 kernel for gpt-medium family; validated numeric drift < 0.2% on our eval set.

2026-02-20 (v2026.02.20) - serving-runtime
- Rolled out GPU affinity improvements to reduce transient OOMs during long sequences.
- Updated: telemetry labels for request-path to include model-variant and quantization tags.

6) Known issues and mitigations

ISSUE-101: Intermittent 502s on long streaming responses
- Symptom: requests streaming > 8k tokens can see 502s during infrequent GC cycles in the node process.
- Root cause: memory fragmentation in tokenizer cache leading to spikes in GC pause.
- Mitigation: restart affected worker, enable streaming shard cap per-worker (worker.streaming_max_tokens=8192), and schedule a patch in next release.

ISSUE-142: Increased p99 after CUDA 12.4 driver upgrade
- Symptom: p99 increased by 18% for quantized INT8 workloads.
- Mitigation: pin to CUDA 12.3 for impacted fleets and schedule kernel vendor triage.

7) Runtime runbooks and incident playbooks

Incident classification
- Sev3: transient latency increases without customer impact (investigate during business hours).
- Sev2: >25% customers see p95 > target for >10 minutes or >5% error rate (oncall page).
- Sev1: sustained outage (>= 30% of requests failing) or major data integrity issue.

Immediate steps (first responder)
1. Acknowledge the page and capture initial blast radius (which regions, affected model-versions).
2. Run quick health checks: kubectl get pods -n serving -l app=worker -o wide; check GPU utilization (dcgm/dmon) and Prometheus: sum(rate(http_requests_total[1m])) by (code).
3. If errors are 5xx and tied to a worker set, triage by restarting the worker(s) with minimal disruption (kubectl rollout restart deployment/<worker-deployment>).
4. If GPU saturation is root cause, enable overflow routing to fallback model-variant: PATCH /admin/routing -d '{"policy":"overflow","fallback":"gpt-medium-8bit"}'
5. If driver/kernel mismatch suspected, fail traffic to canary pool and escalate to runtime infra lead.

Post-incident (owner)
- Create postmortem within 48h, attach profiling artifacts, timeline, and corrective actions. Assign follow-ups and track in the reliability board.

8) Team wiki & onboarding pointers
- Team onboarding checklist: onboarding-checklist.md (internal repo link), include model onboarding template, profiling checklist, and access to the performance-results S3 bucket.
- Helpful pages: serving-runtime-ops-playbook, runtime-architecture-playbook, kernel-scheduling-standards.
- Slack channels: #runtime-ops (primary), #runtime-bench (benchmarks and regressions), #gpu-fleet (capacity & infra).

Appendix A — Example benchmark scenario YAML
---
scenario: gpt-medium-int8-latency
model: gpt-medium-v2
quantization: int8
hardware: a100-80gb
sequence_distribution:
  - length: 32
    pct: 50
  - length: 128
    pct: 30
  - length: 512
    pct: 20
qps: 200
metrics:
  targets:
    p50: 10ms
    p95: 40ms
    p99: 120ms
---

Appendix B — Quick checklist for new model onboarding
1. Run local unit tests and numeric stability checks.
2. Run profiling on canary GPU and collect pprof + Nsight traces.
3. Run benchmarking suite and compare to golden.
4. Validate observability labels and tracing.
5. Deploy with canary percentage 1% -> 10% -> 100% with rollback guardrails.
